7.4.2.10.1 De-authentication
The de-authenticate sub-function shall be always available if service 0x29 is used. This service set the authentication state to deauthenticated for the diagnostic connection the request was received on.
[SWS_Dcm_CONSTR_06095] ⌈The presence of a DcmDsdService with DcmDsdSidTabServiceId set to 0x29, requires a DcmDsdSubService on this DcmDsdService with DcmDsdSubServiceId set to deAuthenticate.⌋
[SWS_Dcm_01561] Deauthentication by diagnostic service request Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04230
⌈On reception of an Authentication (0x29) service with sub-function equal to de-authenticate, the Dcm shall set the authentication state to deauthenticated on the connection the Dcm has received that request.⌋
[SWS_Dcm_01565] Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04230
⌈On reception of an Authentication (0x29) service with sub-function equal to de-Authenticate, the Dcm shall reply with a positive response having the authenticationReturnParameter set to DeAuthentication successful.⌋ The Dcm has an optional distance (mileage) supervision of the authenticated state. In that case the Dcm resets the authenticated state automatically after a certain distance is travelled. The unit of the distance is project specific, the Dcm only compares a distance provided by a data element to an internal configured value. The general idea is to reuse the same distance information that is also provided to the Dem to calculate certain PIDs values. It is recommended to use a definition that is compatible to SAE J1979-DA. AUTOSAR does not define a unit or resolution for the value retrieved by DcmDspAuthenticationMileageInformation. This is intentionally left open as integration aspect, so it allows the Dcm to adapt to any existing distance information. The offset limit defined by DcmDspAuthenticationMileageOffsetLimit needs to take the current resolution into account.
